claims.text: An arc-melted and homogenized high-entropy alloy with titanium and nickel as primary constituents can be prepared as a single-phase solid solution without preexisting secondary phases.
Aging the alloy at approximately 700°C for about 4 hours can trigger in situ TiNi precipitation.
The aging treatment will produce nanoscale TiNi intermetallic precipitates dispersed within the matrix.
Nanoscale TiNi precipitates will act as obstacles to dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by TiNi precipitates will reduce the creep strain rate.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by TiNi precipitates will increase high-temperature yield strength.
The aged alloy will exhibit less creep strain than the unaged alloy.
The aged alloy will exhibit greater high-temperature yield strength than the unaged alloy.
The proposed intervention is applicable to high-entropy alloys in which titanium and nickel are primary constituents.
The proposed intervention is applicable to mechanical testing at approximately 700°C to 800°C.
Testing over approximately 100 hours is sufficient to capture relevant creep behavior.
The exact kinetics and morphology of TiNi precipitation in this high-entropy matrix are uncertain.
Suboptimal aging may cause embrittlement or adverse phase transformations.
A controlled comparison consists of aging one material set at 700°C for 4 hours while retaining another set in the unaged, homogenized condition.
The two sets can be compared by creep testing at 700°C under a fixed stress for 100 hours and by TEM or SEM precipitate characterization.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in creep rate or increase in yield strength relative to the unaged control would falsify the predicted benefit.

contradictions.description: The comparator is called 'as-solidified' in the predicted outcome but 'as-cast, homogenized' elsewhere. Homogenization is a post-solidification treatment, so these labels do not unambiguously specify the same baseline condition.
